active_stack.name: T1_repaired_static_baseline
active_stack.promotion_basis: Pre-June walk-forward plus exchange-fixed June 24-25 matured block both support global-over-time rank.
active_stack.rank_contract_note: Exchange-fixed June 24-25 validation restored both active heads in the candidate universe and removed the stale execution-cache artifact that had made timestamp rank look superior. The causal global-over-time rank reference now has pre-June walk-forward support and a matured later block with identical candidate universe, no duplicate decision keys, and no rank-debug fallback.
active_stack.remaining_validation_item: Static global-over-time T1 remains active. Market-state threshold control has no selected arm after accepted-frontier re-selection; future work must train schedules that recurrently suppress actual baseline-accepted losers directly.

description: Active reliability/portfolio stack: static anchor/meta score with causal global-over-time rank reference after exchange-fixed T1 validation. Market-state controllers remain shadow-only.

later_validation_blocks.interpretation: This later block supports the active timestamp-rank T1 contract over the causal global-rank challenger on the same clean candidate universe, but only covers 9 timestamps and 7-8 accepted trades. Keep timestamp rank provisional and keep accumulating later matured blocks.
later_validation_blocks.name: jun23_00_08_timestamp_vs_global_rank

later_validation_blocks.interpretation: This later block again favors the active timestamp-rank T1 contract over the causal pre-June global-rank challenger, but it still has only 24 timestamps and 10 accepted trades per arm. Keep timestamp rank provisional and keep accumulating later matured blocks.
later_validation_blocks.name: jun23_09_jun24_08_timestamp_vs_global_rank

market_state_controller_validation.deployment_decision: Keep market-state controller disabled/no-op against the global-rank static baseline. The no-backfill candidate passed selection folds but failed three later-window shadow scores, including a June 25-26 window where threshold raises removed profitable short_boll winners. State heads and response diagnostics remain logging/shadow only.

global_rank_threshold_controller_no_back.interpretation: No-backfill threshold overlay remains unsafe: accepted-trade removals do not produce positive full replay economics, and indirect path/capacity effects can remove profitable winners.
No new no-backfill shadow window is scoreable yet under the active global-rank T1 contract; more mature feature/path history is required.

The frozen no-backfill threshold overlay removed only baseline-accepted trades and added no replacements. The action-only/fixed-common-size counterfactual was positive, but full path-dependent replay was negative in the scored later windows because common-trade sizing/path drag was larger. The controller remains shadow-only and should not be promoted without new positive full-replay later-window evidence.
No appendable global-rank no-backfill score window currently exists; next progress requires materializing/scoring a later T1 candidate window after the monitored period.

direct_suppression_combined_shadow_train.interpretation: This model is a diagnostic controller-training surface. Promotion still requires later-window shadow scoring, positive direct suppression recurrence, and full replay gates.

direct_suppression_combined_training_led.interpretation: Combined training evidence for a shadow direct accepted-frontier suppression controller. Later windows are normalized as all accepted rows equal the baseline accepted set; this remains a training artifact, not a promotion.

direct_suppression_shadow_training.interpretation: This model is a diagnostic controller-training surface. Promotion still requires later-window shadow scoring, positive direct suppression recurrence, and full replay gates.

direct_suppression_training_ledger.interpretation: This is a training ledger, not a promotion artifact. It materializes baseline-accepted frontier rows and direct suppression utility so the next controller can learn per-head threshold raises against actual accepted-trade losses instead of replay/path effects.

global_rank_threshold_controller_no_back.interpretation: The earlier no-backfill overlay replay selection is superseded by the accepted-frontier reselection audit. Once post-selection action metrics are no longer allowed to stand in for direct threshold suppression, no controller arm passes. Market-state threshold control remains shadow-only.

global_rank_threshold_controller_smoke.interpretation: The corrected global-rank threshold-controller path executes with market-wide feature-store state inputs and no candidate fallback. This is a one-fold smoke only. The full replay improved the fold, but the post-selection defensive confirmation failed because baseline-accepted suppression sacrificed a winner; no controller is selected or promoted.

global_rank_threshold_controller_walkfor.interpretation: The corrected global-rank threshold controller now runs as a three-fold shadow validation with market-wide feature-store inputs. Overlay replay looks directionally useful, but no executable controller arm passes the strict selection gates because full-replay gains are not recurrent enough and post-selection defensive confirmation is still weak. Keep threshold control shadow-only.

plan_completion_audit.interpretation: The supervised market-state controller artifacts are structurally complete against the active static T1 global-over-time rank contract. Execution remains blocked after adding the June 26 partial shadow window: no controller arm passed strict no-backfill gates, the response layer is support-gated, the strategy-scoped direct-suppression learner still found only a one-fold short_boll best attempt, and later no-backfill shadow monitoring remains negative.

append_window_discovery.interpretation: All currently discovered comparable S2 shadow-controller bundles are already included in the current monitor. No controller append windows are currently available.

shadow_controller_monitor.interpretation: The Jun23-26 S1 accepted-frontier shadow monitor covers three comparable bundles. Artifact audits and schedule safety pass, but coverage, defensive-success, loss-avoided-versus-winner-sacrifice, and recurrence gates fail, so execution remains disabled.

state_head_pruning_audit.interpretation: The current market-state pack is structurally complete but economically sparse: only forecast_h6_shock_up survives leave-one-out, action and defensive-success gates. This supports keeping market-state modulation shadow-only and prevents future priority/rank experiments from consuming the full unpruned state pack as if all heads were validated.
state_head_pruning_audit.shadow_execution_rule: Only active_candidate state heads may feed a future executable threshold controller. Disabled and shadow heads may be logged, inspected and used for research diagnostics, but they must not drive thresholds, ranks, auction priority or sizing without a fresh pruning audit and promotion gate.

strategy_response_quality_gate.interpretation: The active global-rank/no-backfill response layer is structurally valid and signal-positive, but no full two-head arm passes the response-quality gate. short_boll passes for S1/S2/S7, while short_asset is support-blocked by one fold with 25 rows versus the 30-row minimum. Controller activation remains blocked.

t1_timestamp_accepted_frontier_walkforwa.interpretation: Corrected accepted-frontier replay now jumps to the minimum direct accepted-row suppression floor when risk rises. It selected the observed-axes no-backfill overlay as a research candidate, but execution remains blocked until the response support gate and later matured-window validation clear.

t1_timestamp_strategy_response_quality_g.interpretation: T1 timestamp-rank response quality has strong signal for both active heads, but short_asset is support-blocked by one fold with 25 rows versus the 30-row minimum. Since the v3 direct suppressions are mostly short_asset, this remains a rollout blocker despite the positive controller promotion audit.

frontier_action_conservative.interpretation: The stricter action-aware frontier controller becomes effectively no-op at the portfolio level. It validates the fail-closed path but provides no executable lift.

frontier_action_moderate.interpretation: Action-aware frontier thresholding suppresses a small number of candidates with positive candidate-level defensive utility, mostly short_boll, but it does not change accepted trades or portfolio PnL. It remains shadow-only.

market_state_experiment_contract.attribution_note: Supervised market-state and strategy-response ablations must now be evaluated against the active static T1 global-over-time rank contract. Timestamp-rank accepted-frontier artifacts remain historical research evidence and must not be mixed into promotion decisions.
market_state_experiment_contract.name: T1_repaired_static_baseline_experiment_contract

active_timestamp_rank_shadow_validation.interpretation: This directly tests LGBM/XGB market-state head-priority modulation on the active timestamp-rank T1 contract using the broad deployable candidate universe and exact materialized T1 static baselines. Static baseline parity now passes in all 3 windows. The LGBM arm improves June 15-22 by about +21.6 net PnL and XGB by about +10.9, but both accepted-set Jaccards are below the 0.95 production floor and the later Jun 23-24 block worsens full-SL rate. The signal remains useful for research and monitoring, but it is not a production routing rule.

market_state_priority_modulation_validat.deployment_decision: Keep market-state priority modulation shadow-only. It may be logged and rerun on later T1 timestamp-rank and strict global-rank challenger windows, but it must not change active scores, thresholds, ranks or auction ordering until promotion gates pass against exact materialized T1 baselines on recurrent later windows.

exact_t1_timestamp_strict_priority_actio.interpretation: This is the exact materialized T1 timestamp-rank baseline replay with LGBM/XGB market-state priority actions. The best LGBM challenger improves June 15-22 net PnL by about +11.7, reduces full-SL rate, and keeps trade count unchanged, but it changes 10 accepted trades and accepted-set Jaccard is only 0.918 versus the 0.95 strict floor. Keep as shadow evidence that market-state priority can help, not as an active routing rule.

headagnostic_replayaware_selection.interpretation: Head-agnostic replay-aware LGBM/XGB selection on the exchange-fixed June 24-25 global-rank T1 candidate universe selected no learned priority arm. The best replay-aware net-PnL-positive candidate had accepted Jaccard 1.0 and +16.85 net PnL but zero entrants/removed, so it did not prove actionable head-priority routing. Keep market-state priority modulation shadow-only.

exchangefixed_global_rank_shadow_validat.interpretation: After fixing cap-sweep attribution and fitting EV curves on the same global-rank-repaired train-deployable rows as the materialized static baseline, the earlier +4.82 replacement result disappears. Pruned LGBM is only +0.28, pruned XGB is negative, all-state XGB is flat, and all-state LGBM has a small best positive delta but a large negative high-cap tail. No arm passes the opportunity gate. Keep market-state priority modulation shadow-only.

formal_rank_reference_router_validation.interpretation: The formal rank-reference router can express the desired LGBM/XGB market-state modulation layer and improves the June 15-22 development replay, but it does not pass later-window promotion. It must remain shadow-only and must not change live ranks or auction ordering.

global_rank_opportunity_headmix_validati.interpretation: The recurrent selector refuses every global-rank opportunity-priority cap. The fallback safe-cap shadow arm keeps both active heads represented and has very small head-mix movement, so head monoculture is not the blocker. The blocker is recurrent accepted-set action: safe caps only move accepted trades in one of three windows, while the caps that move accepted trades in two windows fail accepted-overlap and timeout gates.

head_priority_assessment.interpretation: June evidence shows short_boll is starved primarily by the global-rank eligibility contract, not by auction ordering alone. The next market-state LGBM/XGB layer should first choose or blend the short_boll rank reference before thresholding, then apply only bounded auction-priority modulation. This remains shadow-only until later-window promotion gates pass.

priority_action_grid_challenger.activation_decision: Do not activate. This proves market-state priority modulation can cross the global-rank auction frontier and add short_boll flow, but the selected June challenger worsens full-SL rate and worst-24h PnL. Keep it as a shadow challenger until recurrent later windows pass stricter risk gates.

strict_replay_gate_validation.interpretation: The same action family can improve June net PnL and add short_boll flow, but no evaluated config passed strict replay gates. The best materialized challenger fails because accepted-set Jaccard is below 0.95 and full-SL rate worsens.

rank_reference_router_plus_priority_vali.interpretation: Applying bounded auction-priority modulation after the state-conditioned rank-reference router does not improve the current evidence. The priority-only arm is small and flat outside development, while rank-plus-priority is worse than T1 on development and later windows. Keep priority modulation disabled.

short_boll_state_rank_scope_switch_shado.activation_decision: Do not activate. Keep static T1 active and keep rank-scope modulation shadow-only until a later untouched matured sequence shows recurrent positive deltas without risk-rate deterioration or excessive accepted-set churn.
short_boll_state_rank_scope_switch_shado.interpretation: The broad-parity shadow replay supports the ranking-starvation hypothesis for short_boll on the June 15-22 development window. Hard global rank starves short_boll and underperforms there; hard state switching improves modestly; the continuous market-state blend from global rank toward timestamp rank improves the development window materially while retaining nonzero global-rank weight. The aggregate June 23-24 validation does not transfer: later-window blend delta is negative, risk rates worsen, and accepted-set overlap is below gate. This remains useful research evidence about state-dependent head priority, but not a production rank-controller.

parallel_validation_artifacts.global_rank_note: Causal pre-June global-over-time rank reference replay using strict PolicyRankReferenceStore lookup with no window-rank fallback. The exchange-fixed June 24-25 validation now supports promoting this rank contract as the static baseline candidate; older timestamp-rank market-state artifacts are stale until rebuilt against global rank.

shadow_only.activation_rule: Do not alter thresholds, scores, ranks or active auction ordering until a controller or priority model is retrained and validated against T1 on fixed universes and incremental portfolio utility.
